chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar from Ali ibn Isma'il from Ali ibn al-Hakam from al-Jahm ibn Abi al-Jahm from Mu'ttab who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me, while prices were rising in Medina: 'How much food do we have?' I said: 'We have enough for many months.' He said: 'Take it out and sell it.' I said: 'There is no food in Medina.' He said: 'Sell it.'
He said: So when I sold it, he said: 'Buy with the people day by day.'

And he said: 'O Mu'ttab, make the sustenance of my family half barley and half wheat, for Allah knows that I am able to feed them pure wheat, but I love that Allah sees me having done well in estimating/providing for the livelihood.'
ai.seo_question: What is the wisdom behind Imam al-Sadiq's advice to mix barley with wheat for his family?
ai.summary: This hadith from the chapter on *Hukra* (withholding essential goods) illustrates Imam al-Sadiq’s strategic use of market dynamics to prevent hoarding and ensure liquidity, even when supply appears scarce. The Imam’s preference for a barley-wheat mix, despite his ability to afford pure wheat, highlights the Shia ethical emphasis on *Ihsan* (excellence in stewardship) and conscious gratitude (*Shukr*) in daily economic practices.
